ConocoPhillips dropped 3.2% today as crude oil prices fell sharply—US oil slid to $89.53 per barrel, down notably from recent highs. While Middle East tensions remain elevated (Iran attacking U.S. military sites, the Strait of Hormuz facing reliability concerns), the market appears to be pricing in enough supply-side risk already. The selloff suggests investors are rotating away from energy or taking profits after the stock climbed 3.3% over three days through November 13.

Oil majors like ConocoPhillips are sensitive to crude price moves in both directions: lower oil doesn't help the profit outlook, even if geopolitical risk keeps some floor under prices. The conflicting headlines—escalating Iran attacks versus a pullback in crude prices—show how fragile the current equilibrium is; any sign that markets are betting on de-escalation or oversupply can quickly undo gains tied to conflict premium.
